title: Mist-CVD gallium oxide access TFT over stacked capacitor
idea: Box: stacked MIM cap x beta-Ga2O3 (4.8 eV) thin-film access transistor x conventional latch SA x BEOL-over-CMOS x Si wafer x atmospheric mist-CVD at <450C. The wide-bandgap channel suppresses thermal generation so off-current falls toward ~1e-20 A/um, and mist-CVD needs no vacuum tool and no indium.
why: Attacks refresh (fact 3): retention moves from 64 ms toward minutes, cutting refresh energy/bandwidth >100x; In-free, low-capex, US-buildable deposition.

title: Nanoelectromechanical relay as zero-leakage DRAM access switch
idea: Box: MIM cap x electrostatic NEMS cantilever relay in a sealed gap x charge-share SA x BEOL monolithic over periphery x Si x sacrificial-layer release with Ru contacts. When open the gap carries essentially zero current, so only capacitor-dielectric leakage remains; ~1-10 ns mechanical closure on a 20 nm gap.
why: Removes the access-transistor leakage tail (fact 3): refresh interval set by dielectric leakage (seconds+), and relays need no tight Vt so wordline can drop below 1 V (fact 10). Contact endurance >1e12 is the risk.

title: Vacuum-channel field-emission nanotriode gates each storage node
idea: Box: stacked cap x lateral ~10 nm vacuum-gap field-emission triode with a hafnium-carbide emitter x current SA x sealed-cavity BEOL tier x Si x self-aligned cavity seal. Below emission threshold the vacuum channel has no band, no generation and no GIDL; a gate pulse thins the barrier for Fowler-Nordheim emission to read/write.
why: Leakage floor set by vacuum, not silicon: retention hours, refresh ~0, and retention becomes temperature-insensitive (fact 3). Emission stability and current density are speculative.

title: Piezoelectronic pressure switch replaces silicon access transistor
idea: Box: MIM cap x piezoelectronic transistor (PMN-PT actuator squeezing a SmSe piezoresistive layer through its insulator-metal transition) x SA x BEOL stack x Si x sputter + anneal. The wordline drives the piezo, pressure drops channel resistance >1e4x; unpowered, the channel is a gapped insulator with no junction to leak.
why: Off-state set by an insulating phase rather than a subthreshold tail (fact 3, ~100x retention) and switching at ~0.1-0.2 V breaks the 3 V wordline floor (fact 10).

title: Ferroelectric domain-wall channel written only during row access
idea: Box: MIM cap x thin-film LiNbO3 where a conducting charged domain wall is nucleated between storage and bitline electrodes x SA x bonded-oxide tier x LNOI wafer x ion-slice bonding. Writing the wall opens a metallic path; erasing it leaves a ~4 eV insulator, so off-state leakage is that of bulk LiNbO3.
why: Wide-gap-insulator isolation pushes refresh toward zero (fact 3); LNOI wafers already come from US photonics lines. Wall nucleation speed and cycling endurance are the risk.

title: Image-sensor 4T pixel gain cell reads 1,000-electron packets
idea: Box: buried-channel storage well (~1-2k e-) x transfer gate + floating-diffusion source follower borrowed from 4T image pixels x correlated-double-sampling column sensing x planar CMOS x Si x CIS fab flow. Full charge transfer onto a tiny floating diffusion gives ~100 uV/e- gain, so a small well replaces the 5 fF capacitor and is written back after read.
why: Escapes the capacitor charge wall (fact 1); buried-channel wells with CIS-grade dark current (few e-/s) extend retention 10-100x (fact 3); reuses existing CIS fab capacity.

title: Double-barrier resonant tunneling access acts as energy filter
idea: Box: InAs quantum-well storage node x AlSb/InAs/AlSb resonant-tunneling two-terminal access x current sense x 4F2 crossbar x GaSb-on-Si x MBE + bonding. Electrons pass only when wordline-bitline bias aligns the resonant level (target on/off >1e6 within ~0.3 V); off resonance the 2 eV AlSb barriers block, so no transistor is needed.
why: Transistor-free 4F2 cell (~1.5x density) with access at ~0.3-0.5 V (fact 10, CV2 ~4x lower) and leakage set by barrier height (fact 3). Valley current and sneak paths are the risk.

title: Mott NDR load-line bistable cell keeps data without refresh
idea: Box: small node cap x one access transistor plus one NbO2 Mott or Si/SiGe Esaki NDR element tied to a hold rail x SA x vertically stacked over the transistor x Si x ALD + anneal. The NDR load line intersecting the leakage line gives two stable node voltages, so leakage self-corrects instead of decaying (tunnel-SRAM idea at ~1T footprint).
why: Eliminates refresh energy and bandwidth (fact 3) entirely; standby set by NDR valley current (target <1 pA/cell). Needs high peak-to-valley ratio at nm scale.

title: Light-pumped self-restoring cell: photodiode gated by its own charge
idea: Box: cap x Si access nMOS x SA x backside-illuminated die under a uniform LED/laser sheet x thinned Si x BSI image-sensor process. Each cell adds a photodiode in series with a tiny transistor gated by the storage node, so a global light flash tops up only nodes that are already high, refreshing the whole array in parallel without any row activation.
why: Refresh energy/bandwidth (fact 3) moves from ~46 fJ/bit bitline CV2 to a few fJ/bit of photons with zero activations, also removing refresh-driven hammer (fact 9). Stray photocurrent into 0-nodes is the risk.

title: Negative-capacitance HZO gate raises access threshold without drive loss
idea: Box: standard pillar cap x recessed-channel access with an HZO negative-capacitance layer over the gate oxide x standard SA x in-array x Si x ALD gate-stack swap. NC voltage amplification gives sub-60 mV/dec swing, so Vt can be raised ~200 mV at the same on-current.
why: ~100x lower subthreshold leakage at equal drive (fact 3), 4-10x less refresh, or same leakage at lower wordline voltage (fact 10).

title: Liquid-nitrogen CXL memory sleds with refresh switched off
idea: Box: unmodified 1T1C dies x standard access at 77 K x standard SA x CXL memory sled immersed in LN2 x Si x no fab change, LN2 piped from on-site air separation. At 77 K junction and subthreshold leakage drop >1e6x so refresh is disabled, and lower wire resistance trims I/O energy.
why: Removes refresh power and bandwidth (fact 3) and permits lower Vt/VPP (fact 10) for pooled capacity; helium-free cryogen. Cryocooling overhead limits it to dense pooled tiers.

title: Test-floor laser anneal heals individual leaky-tail cells
idea: Box: standard cell x standard access x retention test map x post-test die-level repair x Si x picosecond green laser through a BEOL window, like laser fuse repair. Retention test locates the ~0.01% tail cells and a localized pulse anneals trap clusters in that cell's junction, moving it into the main distribution instead of swapping it with redundancy.
why: Tail cells set the 64 ms interval; healing them extends refresh 2-4x (50-75% less refresh energy, fact 3) and frees redundancy area. Reaching the junction through the metal stack is the risk.

title: Resonant LC bitline drive recycles refresh energy adiabatically
idea: Box: standard cell x standard access x SA swung by a resonant LC tank x in-package spiral inductors per bank x Si x standard. During refresh bursts bitline groups swing through the tank so charge oscillates between groups and inductor instead of being dumped to ground, recovering ~60-80% of CV2.
why: Refresh energy (~46 fJ/bit, fact 3) cut 2-4x; same circuit can serve normal activations.

title: Decay-tracking reference voltage widens aged-cell sense margin
idea: Box: standard cell x standard access x SA whose reference comes from a replica cell pair written at the last refresh and leaking in parallel x in-mat x Si x design only. Because true-cell 1s decay while 0s stay, the reference drifts down with the average 1, keeping the decision point midway between a decayed 1 and a 0.
why: Usable signal for aged cells roughly doubles, allowing ~1.5-2x longer refresh interval (fact 3) with no process change.

title: Refresh-free transient zones for AI KV-cache and activations
idea: Box: standard DRAM/HBM x standard access x standard sense x controller tags rows as transient with a write timestamp x system x Si x firmware. Accelerator runtimes guarantee activation and KV-cache blocks are rewritten or freed within 32 ms, so the controller skips refresh on rows written within tRET and on freed rows.
why: Much of HBM holds data younger than tRET; skipping its refresh recovers 10-20% bandwidth and refresh power (fact 3) on the scarcest memory.

title: Helium nanocavity gettering layer beneath DRAM arrays
idea: Box: standard cell x standard access x SA x array-wide buried layer x Si x MeV He implant + anneal forming nanocavities ~1 um below junctions. Cavity walls trap Fe, Cu and Ni that create mid-gap generation centers in storage junctions, the origin of many tail cells.
why: Shrinks the retention tail (fact 3) 2-5x; uses milligram-scale helium, negligible against the Qatar-constrained supply.

title: Charge-plasma storage junction: no dopants, no implant damage
idea: Box: cap x access transistor whose storage-side n-region is induced electrostatically by a low-work-function metal contact and a positive fixed-charge dielectric instead of implanted phosphorus x SA x in-array x thin-body Si x ALD. With no metallurgical junction there is no end-of-range damage or dopant cluster to host trap-assisted tunneling.
why: Removes the main junction-leakage and GIDL tail sites (fact 3), aiming at ~10x tail reduction, and deletes implant steps.

title: Silicon-on-nothing void under every storage junction
idea: Box: cap x recessed access x SA x in-array x bulk Si with empty-space-in-silicon cavities x shallow trench array + high-temperature H2 anneal that migrates Si to seal a void beneath each storage diffusion. The junction bottom, usually the largest generation volume, now faces vacuum instead of depleted silicon.
why: Junction leakage (fact 3) cut 3-5x by area removal; lower junction capacitance also improves charge-transfer ratio.

title: Two-nanometre quantum-confined silicon body widens the access bandgap
idea: Box: cap x <=2.5 nm Si nanosheet access channel x SA x lateral 3D-stackable cell x epitaxial Si/SiGe superlattice x selective SiGe etch. Confinement raises the effective gap ~0.3-0.4 eV, dropping intrinsic carrier density ~100x and band-to-band tunneling sharply, while staying in silicon.
why: Order-of-magnitude cut in generation and GIDL leakage (fact 3) without new channel materials, compatible with Si/SiGe-stack 3D DRAM (fact 2).

title: Series lock gate: second gate per channel shared by subarray
idea: Box: cap x vertical channel with two stacked gates (row wordline + a subarray-wide lock gate nearest the storage node) x SA x in-array 3D x Si x second gate tier deposited in the same trench. The lock gate stays deeply negative except when its subarray is active, adding a series stack that multiplies isolation.
why: Stack effect plus deeper off-bias cuts leakage 10-100x in idle subarrays (most of the chip), extending their refresh (fact 3) and blocking hammer coupling into them (fact 9).

title: Direct-tunneling charge-trap cell with second-scale retention
idea: Box: charge in a SiN/HfO2 trap layer x 1.5-2 nm tunnel oxide written by direct tunneling (not Fowler-Nordheim) x gain-transistor sensing x in-array x Si x ALD gate stack. Direct tunneling at ~1.5 V writes in ~10 ns without the high-field damage that limits flash endurance, while trap depth gives seconds of retention.
why: Refresh ~100x rarer (fact 3), no capacitor (fact 1), sub-2 V operation (fact 10); endurance target >1e15 since no hot carriers.

title: Inline e-beam voltage contrast maps junction leakage before capacitor
idea: Box: standard cell x access transistor probed at storage-contact level x e-beam voltage-contrast imaging of charge decay per contact x inline metrology x Si x fab method. Charging each exposed storage contact and imaging its decay over ms maps the leakage distribution on every wafer, feeding implant/anneal recipes in days rather than months of electrical test.
why: Faster learning on the leakage tail (fact 3) shortens yield ramps for new nodes and new US fabs, reducing capital time (fact 4).

title: Coulomb-blockade silicon dot holds bit behind charging energy
idea: Box: few-electron Si quantum dot (<3 nm) storage x wordline-gated tunnel barrier access x single-electron-transistor electrometer sensing x in-array x SOI x oxidation-thinned nanowire. The dot's charging energy (>10 kT at room temperature for sub-3 nm dots) blocks electron escape until the wordline lowers the barrier.
why: Charge per bit drops from ~30,000 e- to ~10 e-, slashing CV2 (fact 10) and sidestepping the capacitor wall (fact 1). Room-temperature variability is speculative.

title: One shallow p+ pinning implant mask ends storage-node surface leakage
idea: Box: standard cap x standard access x standard SA x in-array x Si x exactly one added implant mask. Borrowing the image-sensor pinned photodiode, a shallow p+ layer over the exposed storage-node diffusion pins the Si/SiO2 interface in hole accumulation so its interface states stop generating current.
why: Pinning cut CIS dark current ~100x; surface generation is a major tail source, so expect 3-10x lower tail leakage and proportional refresh savings (fact 3) for one mask.

title: GaP epitaxy in existing storage contacts puts field in wide-gap material
idea: Box: standard cap x access with a Si/GaP heterojunction storage drain x standard SA x in-array x Si x selective GaP MOCVD inside the already-opened storage-node contact holes (zero added masks). GaP is lattice-matched to Si (0.4%) with a 2.26 eV gap, so the gate-edge high-field region sits where band-to-band tunneling is negligible.
why: GIDL and trap-assisted tunneling dominate the tail (fact 3); a wide-gap drain could cut them >10x with no new mask. Antiphase defects and thermal budget are the risk.

title: Deliberately weakened canary cells let dies refresh at true retention
idea: Box: standard cell x canary cells with a leakier access transistor made by one extra Vt-lowering implant mask x on-die canary sensing x per bank x Si x one mask. Canaries fail at ~1/4 of the weakest real cell's retention, so the die stretches its interval until canaries start failing, tracking temperature, voltage and aging live.
why: Replacing worst-case spec with live tracking typically allows 2-4x longer intervals, cutting refresh energy and bandwidth loss (fact 3) 50-75%.

title: Leakage-balanced bitline standby voltage cancels junction loss
idea: Box: standard cell x standard access x retuned SA precharge generator x in-array x Si x zero masks. In self-refresh the bitlines park slightly above VDD/2 so subthreshold current flows into 1-nodes and offsets their junction/GIDL loss, while 0-nodes absorb the small extra leak from their larger margin; the park voltage is trimmed per die at test.
why: Balancing the two failure tails extends worst-case retention ~1.5-2x (fact 3) with only a trimmable regulator.

title: Segmented cell plate dips during idle to relax junction field
idea: Box: standard cap x standard access x SA x in-array x Si x one mask that cuts the common cell plate into per-subarray segments. Idle subarrays lower their plate ~0.2-0.3 V, coupling all storage nodes down and reducing reverse bias and gate-edge field on 1-nodes; the plate is restored before activation.
why: GIDL/TAT fall exponentially with field: ~3-5x retention in idle subarrays (fact 3) for one mask.

title: Supercritical CO2 deuterium passivation at 250C, no masks
idea: Box: standard cell x standard access x SA x whole-wafer post-BEOL treatment x Si x supercritical CO2 carrying D2/D2O at ~250C and >100 bar. The supercritical fluid penetrates dense metal stacks to reach junction and gate-oxide traps that forming-gas anneals miss, and Si-D bonds resist thermal/hot-carrier depassivation better than Si-H.
why: Shrinks and stabilizes the tail, including variable retention time (fact 3), with zero masks on cheap US-buildable tools.

title: Wordline topography shadows tilted halo implant, zero added masks
idea: Box: standard cap x asymmetric access transistor x SA x in-array x Si x high-tilt implant in which the existing wordline/hardmask stack shadows the storage side. Only the bitline side receives the halo dose, so the storage junction stays lightly doped and low-field while short-channel control is kept.
why: Lower storage-junction field cuts TAT/GIDL tail 3-5x (fact 3) without the usual dedicated asymmetric-implant mask.

title: One-mask selective reoxidation thickens storage-side gate edge
idea: Box: standard cap x recessed access with asymmetric gate dielectric x SA x in-array x Si x one mask exposing only storage-side recess tops to an extra radical oxidation. Thicker dielectric only where the gate overlaps the storage junction lowers the field driving GIDL while channel oxide stays thin for drive.
why: GIDL is exponential in field; ~30% thicker edge oxide can cut it ~10x, extending refresh (fact 3) for one mask.

title: Barrier-free molybdenum buried wordline recessed deeper, tungsten-free
idea: Box: standard cap x buried-channel access with barrier-less Mo wordline x SA x in-array x Si x CVD/ALD Mo using the existing recess pattern (zero added masks). Mo's low narrow-line resistivity without a TiN liner lets the conductor sit further below the storage junction at equal wordline resistance, shrinking gate-storage overlap.
why: Reduced overlap lowers GIDL ~3-5x (fact 3) and removes tungsten (China ~80%) from the densest layer.

title: Self-aligned dipole layer raises threshold only near storage node
idea: Box: standard cap x buried-channel access with an Al2O3 dipole interlayer added after a partial wordline recess x SA x in-array x Si x recess-deposit-etchback on existing patterns (zero masks). The dipole shifts local Vt ~+0.3 V only in the upper gate segment beside the storage junction, while the lower channel keeps low Vt for drive.
why: Higher off-state barrier exactly where leakage originates: ~10x lower subthreshold/GIDL leakage (fact 3) without drive loss.

title: Neutral-beam etch of wordline recess removes plasma-induced traps
idea: Box: standard cap x recessed access x SA x in-array x Si x neutral-beam (charge-free, VUV-free) etch replacing RIE for the recess trench, zero masks. Neutral beams avoid the charging and VUV photon damage that seed interface traps on the trench walls forming the channel and storage-junction edge.
why: Fewer interface traps shrink the subthreshold/TAT tail and Vt spread (fact 3), targeting ~2x retention on the same mask set.

title: Deep boron barrier implant blocks substrate diffusion leakage
idea: Box: standard cap x standard access x SA x in-array x Si x one high-energy implant mask placing a p+ layer ~0.5-1 um below the array. Its built-in field reflects electrons diffusing from the substrate and periphery (including sense-amp hot-carrier emission) away from storage nodes.
why: Diffusion current dominates at 85-95C; blocking it gives ~2x hot retention (fact 3) and less periphery-induced disturb for one mask.

title: Zero-majority row encoding plus refresh skip for empty rows
idea: Box: standard cell x standard access x SA with per-row invert flag and all-discharged flag x in-mat logic x Si x zero masks. Rows are written inverted when that leaves fewer charged (leak-vulnerable) cells, and rows flagged all-discharged are skipped by refresh since discharged true cells cannot decay.
why: Zero pages and sparse AI tensors are common; skipping them and halving charged cells elsewhere cuts refresh energy 20-50% and retention-failure exposure (fact 3).

title: OS free-page list drives row-granular partial refresh
idea: Box: standard DRAM x standard access x standard sense x per-row refresh-enable bitmap inside the DRAM written by the OS allocator via mode-register commands x system x Si x zero masks. Freed or never-allocated pages stop being refreshed; the OS zeroes them on allocation anyway.
why: Servers often have 20-50% of DRAM free or reclaimable; row-level partial refresh cuts refresh power/bandwidth proportionally (fact 3).

title: Buy retention-reject dies and run them in fast-refresh CXL pools
idea: Box: commodity dies that failed 64 ms retention x standard access x standard sense x CXL expander controller with 8-16 ms refresh and per-row remap x system x Si x zero masks. A company buys downgraded dies at scrap prices, profiles them, and sells pooled CXL capacity where extra refresh is hidden by bank parallelism.
why: Raises usable supply by reclaiming a few % of output now scrapped or downgraded, with zero fab capital (capital intensity, supply).

title: JEDEC retention-map register and per-row refresh command
idea: Box: standard cell x standard access x standard sense x vendor-measured retention class per row group exposed in a readable register plus a targeted-row refresh command x controller multi-rate refresh x Si x zero masks. Policy: push the standard through JEDEC and require it in CHIPS-funded and federal procurement so every vendor ships it.
why: Most rows retain >1 s; multi-rate refresh cuts refresh 70%+ (fact 3) but has been blocked by missing vendor data, which a standard unlocks.

title: Aerogel thermal break keeps HBM DRAM cores 15C cooler
idea: Box: standard HBM core dies x standard access x standard sense x silica-aerogel or porous-polymer layer between hot logic base die and core stack, with logic heat routed through dedicated copper thermal TSVs to the lid x package x Si x zero masks. Core dies then sit near cold-plate temperature instead of the logic hotspot.
why: Retention halves per ~10C; a 15C drop gives ~3x longer refresh interval, reclaiming HBM bandwidth and power (facts 3, 6).

title: In-field wordline self-heating anneal heals variable-retention traps
idea: Box: standard cell x access transistor used as its own heater via ms high-current wordline pulses during idle x SA retention self-test x in-mat x Si x zero masks. Local ~200-300C channel micro-anneals relax metastable trap configurations behind variable retention time, then a self-test confirms the row.
why: VRT cells force conservative refresh margins; healing them in the field could extend refresh ~2x (fact 3). Thermal damage risk is speculative.

title: One-mask BEOL thermistor grid sets refresh per subarray
idea: Box: standard cell x standard access x SA x vanadium-oxide thin-film thermistor grid patterned by one added mask above the arrays x per-subarray refresh timers x Si. Each subarray's refresh rate follows its local temperature instead of the hottest die sensor.
why: On-die gradients reach 10-20C in HBM/3D stacks; local rates cut average refresh 30-60% (fact 3) for one mask.

title: Bank-to-bank bitline charge recycling during refresh bursts
idea: Box: standard cell x standard access x SA x charge-transfer switches linking bitlines of two banks refreshed in antiphase x in-array design x Si x zero masks. When bank A finishes restore, its high-side bitline charge is shared into bank B's bitlines before discharge, reusing up to half the swing charge.
why: Refresh energy (~46 fJ/bit, fact 3) and VARY supply current cut ~30-40% with only switches and timing.

title: Self-referenced slow sensing during refresh rescues decayed cells
idea: Box: standard cell x standard access x SA run in two-step self-reference only during refresh (read and hold bitline level, write a known 1, read again, compare) x in-mat x Si x zero masks. Comparing the cell with itself removes capacitor and offset mismatch, so cells decayed to ~25% of signal still resolve; normal reads stay fast.
why: Refresh need only catch cells before ~75% decay instead of ~50%, allowing ~2x longer intervals (fact 3); the extra latency hides in background refresh.

title: Neighbor wordlines driven deeper negative while a row is open
idea: Box: standard cell x standard access x SA x sub-wordline drivers given a second negative rail selected for rows N+-1 during row N activation x in-array x Si x zero masks. The extra ~-0.3 V on adjacent wordlines cancels coupling and passing-gate effects that transiently open neighbor access transistors.
why: Cuts activation-induced leakage that erodes neighbor retention and drives row hammer (facts 3, 9): ~2x retention under heavy traffic, higher hammer threshold.

title: Solar-cell Al2O3 negative-charge liner passivates isolation sidewalls
idea: Box: standard cap x standard access x SA x in-array x Si x ALD Al2O3 STI liner carrying ~-5e12 cm-2 fixed charge (the PERC solar-cell trick) replacing the oxide liner, zero masks. The negative charge accumulates holes on the trench sidewall next to the storage junction, field-effect passivating edge interface states.
why: STI-edge generation is a known tail source; this passivation cut solar surface recombination ~10x, so expect 2-5x tail reduction (fact 3).
